description: Single filer born January 1, 1961: by the tax rule 65 at the end of 2025 (reaches 65 the day before the birthday), so the additional standard deduction and the full senior deduction apply.
worked:
Filing status: single.
Taxpayer: born 1961-01-01, age 65 at the end of 2025.
Form 1040: line 1z wages 60,000.
Form 1040 line 9 total income = 60,000 = 60,000; line 10 adjustments 0; line 11a/11b adjusted gross income = 60,000.
Line 12e standard deduction = 15,750 basic (single) + 1 x 2,000 additional (unmarried amount, one per box checked on line 12d for age 65 or older / blind) = 17,750.
Schedule 1-A: line 1 = line 11b 60,000; line 3 MAGI = 60,000 (no excluded income).
  Part V: line 31 = 60,000; line 32 = 75,000; line 33: 60,000 - 75,000 is zero or less, so line 35 = 6,000
  line 36a (born before January 2, 1961) = 6,000; line 37 = 6,000 -> line 38 -> Form 1040 line 13b
Line 14 = 17,750 + 6,000 = 23,750; line 15 taxable income = 60,000 - 23,750 = 36,250.
Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax): Tax Rate Schedule X (single) on 36,250: 10% x 11,925 = 1,192.50; 12% x (36,250 - 11,925) = 2,919; total 4,111.50
Form 8960: lines 8 and 12 net investment income = 0; line 13 MAGI = 60,000; line 14 threshold = 200,000; line 15 = 60,000 - 200,000, zero or less, so 0; line 17 net investment income tax = 0.
Form 8959 Part I: line 1 Medicare wages (W-2 box 5) = line 4 = 60,000; line 5 = 200,000 (single); line 6 = 60,000 - 200,000, zero or less, so 0; line 7 = 0.9% x 0 = 0 (additional Medicare tax).
Total tax = 4,111.50 regular + 0 net investment income tax + 0 additional Medicare tax = 4,111.50.
